thread.title_full: Wisconsin collected 10.6% less in taxes on amusements license taxes in 2024 than in previous year

author: The Sconi
title: Wisconsin collected 10.6% less in taxes on amusements license taxes in 2024 than in previous year
text:
Out of the $25.5 billion in total tax revenue collected by Wisconsin in 2024, $76,000 came from amusements license taxes, representing a decrease from the previous year, when the total was $85,000, according to the U.S. Census Bureau’s Annual Survey of State Government Tax Collections (STC).
The State Government Tax Collections (STC) survey tracks five major tax categories and up to 25 subcategories, gathering data from all 50 state governments and their dependent agencies.
The Census Bureau notes that it defines tax classifications consistently across states, which may differ from how individual states categorize them.
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, state and local governments collect a wide range of taxes to fund public programs and services. These revenues are typically allocated to areas such as transportation, education, and public safety. In 2024, state tax collections alone amounted to nearly $1.5 trillion nationwide, representing a significant part of overall government operations.
The amount each state collects depends on its tax rates, bases, and policy priorities. In 2023, North Dakota topped the list with the largest state tax collection per capita at $7,715.71, followed by Hawaii ($7,098.72) and Vermont ($6,948.15), according to the U.S. Census Bureau.
Below is a breakdown of how taxes were classified by subcategory and how much was collected.

| General sales and gross receipts taxes | $7,747,108,000 | $7,456,088,000 |
| Corporation net income taxes | $3,370,905,000 | $2,667,937,000 |
| Selective sales and gross receipts taxes | $2,894,325,000 | $2,900,188,000 |
| Motor fuels sales taxes | $1,095,905,000 | $1,177,749,000 |
| Motor vehicle license taxes | $758,033,000 | $714,690,000 |
| Other selective sales and gross receipts taxes | $520,670,000 | $433,173,000 |
| Tobacco products sales taxes | $492,349,000 | $540,130,000 |
| Public utilities sales taxes | $420,227,000 | $419,402,000 |
| Occupation and businesses license taxes | $389,520,000 | $349,445,000 |
| Insurance premiums sales taxes | $287,839,000 | $251,916,000 |
| Documentary and stock transfer taxes | $88,823,000 | $98,757,000 |
| Alcoholic beverages sales taxes | $77,166,000 | $77,641,000 |
| Hunting and fishing license taxes | $65,979,000 | $69,556,000 |
| Public utilities license taxes | $57,139,000 | $50,067,000 |
| Other license taxes | $50,719,000 | $58,378,000 |
| Motor vehicle operators license taxes | $41,721,000 | $38,358,000 |
| Corporations in general license taxes | $30,810,000 | $31,804,000 |
| Other taxes, NEC | $18,084,000 | $17,430,000 |
| Alcoholic beverages license taxes | $2,398,000 | $2,519,000 |
| Severance taxes | $2,024,000 | $2,186,000 |
| Amusements sales taxes | $169,000 | $177,000 |
| Amusements license taxes | $76,000 | $85,000 |
